notes.note: Research date: 2026-10-08. All entries are proposed mappings, not implemented or runtime-verified claims. expectedSupport is a stage acceptance target derived from declarations; requires-investigation is an explicit unresolved cell.

Extraction uses the exact published native declaration export graph, locally referenced payload/configuration types, generated style fields/operators, explicit experimental shape animator declarations, and RN0.87.1 inherited ViewProps/NativeMethods. Internal React component lifecycle/bridge machinery is inventoried with internal disposition.

The iOS dependency is a wrapper-supported range (~>11.23.1), not an exact resolved SDK pin. A lockfile/build must record the selected SDK before final baseline acceptance. Android SDK default is exact11.23.1.

Native download tokens are no longer required by RNMapbox10.3.7: rnmapbox-maps.podspec documents deprecated RNMapboxMapsDownloadToken; plugin/src/withMapbox.ts declares the download token deprecated and creates an unauthenticated Maven repository unless explicitly given a legacy token. Runtime public access token is separate.

RNMapbox10.3.7 requires React Native New Architecture and Mapbox v11; old architecture and Mapbox v10 are rejected in the podspec. Native RN0.87.1 integration still requires compilation and runtime evidence.

MarkerView10.3.7 documents live React Native child press feedback on both platforms. Android-only stopGesturePropagation opts children out of map gestures; its runtime composition needs verification. Live marker dragging is not declared directly; missing draggable prop does not establish a renderer limitation.

RasterArraySource tileSize and bounds are documented as Android direct options and iOS TileJSON-derived values. Preserve requested behavior using TileJSON where possible and investigate remaining option contracts rather than silently dropping fields.

Camera.triggerKey is explicitly documented as not yet implemented. Strict controlled camera requires real acceptance/rejection/clamping evidence; Camera props alone do not prove the common controlled contract.

Wrapper Style component documents only sources/layers and silently ignores other root fields. one-map-react must route full style documents through owned Map style configuration or reject explicit unsupported options; this wrapper omission does not constrain SDK style-root support.

Offline legacy aliases and cache operations require runtime investigation: documentation includes pre-v10 deprecations, while the frozen baseline is v11. Do not label a stale declaration as successful v11 support.

EXCLUDED: arbitrary native SDK APIs not exported or forwarded by RNMapbox are outside this wrapper inventory. Applicable SDK style schemas/property/operator support are reconciled during S08, alongside public wrapper fields.
REQUIRED IMPLEMENTATION EVIDENCE: platform differences are flagged from declarations; feature-stage native bridge review and runtime/physical-device behavior establish final conformance.
REQUIRED IMPLEMENTATION EVIDENCE: source-linked schema fields have generated declaration signatures; S08 verifies pinned SDK schemas, property removal, defaults and expression behavior.
Package subpath/tooling, native build configuration and Expo plugin options are inventoried separately from React component props.

Primary integration reassigned host styling, press events, style/source schemas, ornaments, constants and experimental animators to their actual feature-stage owners. S02 owns only portable foundation values and bridge-type rationale; feature implementation and runtime checks remain with those feature stages.
This is a source/declaration inventory, not runtime compatibility evidence. All feature implementations and runtime verification remain pending.

Mapbox commit download returned HTTP 404. The public v3.32.0 tag source and npm 3.32.0 declarations were inspected; Mapbox source citations use the pinned release tag. Confirm the supplied commit before replacing tag citations.
MapLibre style-spec 26.4.4 is the exact dependency recorded in maplibre-gl 6.13.0 package-lock.json, not an arbitrary latest style schema.

The TypeScript checker resolves inherited properties and union alternatives against published renderer declarations. A transported schema field is inventoried without claiming wrapper or cross-platform runtime parity.
CSSProperties is resolved with the selected @types/react 19.3.0 host baseline and csstype 3.2.3; host style fields serve Map, Marker, and Popup without duplicating every CSS field three times.

The distinct /mapbox-legacy entrypoint is recorded as composition through the selected stable Mapbox 3 adapter. Legacy Mapbox 1/2 compatibility is outside this current-stable release baseline; this is a project version boundary, not an SDK feature limitation.

Wrapper MapRef declarations include renderer fields that createRef does not copy at runtime. Such declaration-only fields are flagged for investigation rather than represented as working forwarded properties.

Private/underscore renderer implementation members are excluded. Underscore declarations exposed by wrapper type aliases need audit for accidental public leakage; SDK ownership escapes cannot substitute for assigned common features.

Renderer source/control/handler object members are included because getSource, getStyle, map handlers, and control refs can expose them. Host DOM methods are retained as host-specific typed extension paths, not portable native operations.

Overloads share a coverage entry. Upstream APIs retain their signatures in the pinned declaration/source links; inventory presence does not validate default values, return timing, event ordering, or option interactions.

Primitive and tuple/array type-alternative prototype methods are excluded from field enumeration: ordinary JavaScript string/array operations are not independent mapping SDK features. Named coordinate/option aliases remain inventoried, including SDK class methods when the alias includes a class alternative.

This inventory records declarations and documented contracts, not verified adapter or SDK runtime support. All support cells must start unverified. No wrapper omission has been classified as unsupported.

Pinned wrapper commit 059f46b2dc728fb6259af91b27a071bcda19a2ae resolves v11.5.0. All declared index exports are indexed, public type fields inherited from wrapper/RN declarations are expanded, module methods are indexed, and style-spec26.2.1 fields/operators are enumerated separately.

Android default is org.maplibre.gl:android-sdk-opengl:13.6.1 with annotation/scalebar plugins3.0.2, turf6.0.1 and okhttp4.12.0. Dependencies resolve through public Maven Central/google repositories; pinned build.gradle has no authenticated download repository or secret download token requirement. Source: https://github.com/maplibre/maplibre-react-native/blob/059f46b2dc728fb6259af91b27a071bcda19a2ae/package/android/build.gradle and https://github.com/maplibre/maplibre-react-native/blob/059f46b2dc728fb6259af91b27a071bcda19a2ae/package/android/gradle.properties

iOS default MLRN_NATIVE_VERSION6.31.0 uses SPM exactVersion6.31.0 from https://github.com/maplibre/maplibre-gl-native-distribution with product MapLibre; MLRN.post_install injects package dependency. Pinned podspec contains no secret download credential requirement. Custom SPM/repositories or tile providers may have independent authentication. Source: https://github.com/maplibre/maplibre-react-native/blob/059f46b2dc728fb6259af91b27a071bcda19a2ae/package/MapLibreReactNative.podspec
MapLibre setup needs no Mapbox token. MAPBOX_PUBLIC_TOKEN is for selected Mapbox resource/runtime tests; provider credentials are distinct from SDK download credentials.

New architecture only; package peer floors RN>=0.80.0 and React>=19.1.0. Exact inherited host fields use selected RN0.87.1 artifact. RN host inherited props/styles preserve host-specific API through documented forwarding and require per-component/platform validation.

Android source minSdkVersion24 overrides getting-started documentation's stated>=23; compileSdk35/targetSdk34/kotlin2.0.21 are source defaults. SDK override settings require conformance beyond this frozen default.

Native platform differences requiring tests: Android touchZoom=false also disables doubleTapZoom/doubleTapHoldZoom; Android scaleBarPosition supports top-left only; androidView surface/texture is Android only; frame scheduling is preferred on iOS and maximum on Android; live Marker.selected is iOS-only; ViewAnnotation Android children are bitmaps and iOS Callout requires title; NativeUserLocation course differs on iOS and Android.

GeoJSONSource feature-state drops null object keys while retaining null array elements; absent state returns null; removals apply next rendered frame. Vector source queries cover currently loaded tiles within viewport; GeoJSON getData has distinct data semantics. S11/S25 must reconcile these with portable contracts.

Location default Android engine is documented as not working on emulator; google engine supports emulator but changes provider/build dependencies. LocationManager permissions request Android fine/coarse or iOS when-in-use; map mounting must not silently start tracking.

Known inventory boundaries: arbitrarily recursive GeoJSON/ReactNode values are represented by their public value contract rather than every recursive field; actual native React component handles are covered by typed handle/animation ownership contracts rather than every internal implementation method. Nested RN event payloads and inherited opaque animated value internals may need additional explicit rows if they expose an independent application task. Schema operator overload syntax and sdk-support metadata are linked rather than expanded into a row per overload. Runtime feasibility for native controlled camera/live dragging/popups remains assigned to S12/S13b/S15; this inventory does not claim them impossible.

Primary integration reassigned host styling, press events, style/source schemas, ornaments, constants and experimental animators to their actual feature-stage owners. entries.documentation: /** * Whether this view needs to rendered offscreen and composited with an alpha in order to preserve 100% correct colors and blending behavior. * The default (false) falls back to drawing the component and its children * with an alpha applied to the paint used to draw each element instead of rendering the full component offscreen and compositing it back with an alpha value. * This default may be noticeable and undesired in the case where the View you are setting an opacity on * has multiple overlapping elements (e.g. multiple overlapping Views, or text and a background). * * Rendering offscreen to preserve correct alpha behavior is extremely expensive * and hard to debug for non-native developers, which is why it is not turned on by default. * If you do need to enable this property for an animation, * consider combining it with renderToHardwareTextureAndroid if the view contents are static (i.e. it doesn't need to be redrawn each frame). * If that property is enabled, this View will be rendered off-screen once, * saved in a hardware texture, and then composited onto the screen with an alpha each frame without having to switch rendering targets on the GPU. */
